chunks: When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was prevented, a man came to him and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am a wealthy man, meaning one with much property, and I am in a town where no one but I can properly manage my wealth. So inform me, O Messenger of Allah, of something which, if I do it, I would have the like of the pilgrim’s reward.”

He said to him: “Look at the mountain,” meaning Abū Qubays, “if you were to spend the like of this in gold, giving it as charity in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, you would still not attain the reward of the pilgrim.”

key_terms.أَبَا قُبَيْسٍ: Abū Qubays, the mountain being referred to
key_terms.أَجْرِ ٱلْحَاجِّ: the reward of the pilgrim performing hajj
key_terms.ذَهَبًا: gold, used here to indicate immense wealth
key_terms.صُدَّ: was prevented or turned back from proceeding
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; for His cause
key_terms.ٱلْجَبَلِ: the mountain pointed to as a visible comparison

ai.seo_question: Can charity equal the reward of hajj in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the unique merit of hajj and teaches that its reward cannot simply be equaled by financial expenditure, even if that expenditure is immense and sincerely given in the way of Allah. It also reflects a historical moment when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was prevented from continuing, while still affirming the distinct spiritual station of the pilgrim.
